subject: Optimo onboarding — tuning plan & kickoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: James Park <james@optimo.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Optimo onboarding — tuning plan & kickoff

Hi James / Elena,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, we put together a short Mutual Action Plan focused on cost & performance tuning during the onboarding window — specifically: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile selection, and routing policies (latency vs cost tiers). I attached an initial implementation plan (optimo-implementation-mtaplan.pdf) and a rough quantization matrix for the models you've selected.

Key asks from your side before the kickoff:
- Representative sample of 100 requests (anonymized) showing typical token lengths and response shapes
- Expected peaks: qps and 95th latency targets for both interactive and batch scenarios
- Any compliance constraints for KV caching (TTL, PII rules)

Proposed kickoff: next Tuesday 2026-07-06 10:00am PT — 60 minutes. Agenda in the attachment.

Next steps I recommend: we run a lightweight sweep (1-2 days) on three quantization profiles (int8, q4_0, q4_1) and two batching targets (prefetch 16 / 64) against your typical prompt distribution to show cost/latency tradeoffs. Our SRE will also test prefix cache hit rates with a 48-hour synthetic window to estimate unit token savings.

Sharing the HubSpot deal and Drive links in metadata below. If that all sounds good I'll send the calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
(jordan@redwood.com)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

James — quick notes on sanitization and what we need for accurate measurements:

- For caching: keep full prompt prefix/token boundaries but remove any PII fields (names, emails, account IDs). If you replace PII with consistent tokens (e.g., <USER_1>) that preserves hit behavior.
- For latency/cost sweep: we need per-request token counts (prompt + expected completion) and a binary flag for whether responses are streaming or full.
- For quantization analysis: sample model logits aren't necessary; just provide sample inputs and expected output lengths. We'll run model variants under the hood on our infra.

I've attached a small example of a kv cache distribution we like to use (kv_cache_example.png) and a checklist for data deliverables.

If APAC times are needed, Jordan — can you propose 2 alternatives? I can align SRE availability.

Ava Chen
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding some logistics and the proposed kickoff agenda:

Proposed kickoff agenda (60 min):
- 0-5 min: Introductions & goals (Jordan)
- 5-20 min: Optimo workload profile and constraints (James / Elena)
- 20-35 min: Redwood proposed sweep: batching, cache TTLs, quant profiles (Ava)
- 35-50 min: Routing policy discussion — latency vs cost tiers & fallback behaviors (Connor)
- 50-60 min: Action items & owners (all)

Deliverables within 7 business days post-kickoff:
- A: Tuning sweep report with 3 profiles and cost/latency matrix
- B: Recommended production config (batch sizes, cache TTLs, quant profile) and rollout plan (canary->full)
- C: Cost delta estimate (monthly) for chosen config vs baseline

I put tentative time on the calendar for Tue 2026-07-06 10:00am PT; alternative APAC slot: Wed 2026-07-07 02:00am SGT (we can flip to a later APAC-friendly slot if you prefer).

Subject: Re: Optimo onboarding — tuning plan & kickoff

Thanks — we can take Tue 10am PT. A couple of clarifying constraints to surface ahead of time:

- Cost target: we want at least a 25% reduction in per-token spend vs our current hosted endpoint within the first 30 days post-rollout, without moving to a lower-quality model.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 350ms for interactive paths; batch jobs can be up to 2s.
- Cache policy: no persistent storage of substrings of user PII; opt-in only. TTLs must be configurable per-customer segment.

One more question: can you share an example of tradeoffs between int8 vs q4_1 for our model family? We have a hard requirement to not regress on coherence for longer completions.

—Elena
Product Ops, Optimo AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@optimo.ai>, James Park <james@optimo.ai>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, accounts@optimo.ai
Date: Sat, 03 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optimo onboarding — tuning plan & kickoff

Elena / James — perfect, appreciate the clarity. Quick replies to your constraints/questions and the agreed plan: 

- Cost target: we'll prioritize the batch/quant sweep to surface the best config that meets your 25% cost reduction target. Historically for similar families, q4_1 with a 32-token batching sweet spot hit ~20-30% savings with <3% quality delta on long completions; int8 often gives more savings but sometimes requires a small temperature/decoding tweak to maintain coherence. We'll include the exact examples in the sweep report. See redwood-quant-matrix.csv for baseline reference.
- Latency SLO: we'll run 95th percentile checks across the sweep and include a recommended routing policy: interactive requests routed to low-latency pool (no batching, higher cost) and background/batch routed to a denser quantized pool with larger batch windows. We'll provide a canary rollout plan with automatic fallback to hosted API if any regression exceeds your SLAs.
- Cache policy: understood. We'll provide a config template that allows per-segment TTL and an opt-in toggle for persisted cache; default will be ephemeral KV with policy-based masking of PII.

Action items agreed:
1) Optimo: deliver 100-sample dataset + peak qps details by EOD Friday (2026-07-02).
2) Redwood: run sweep (3 quant profiles x 2 batching regimes) and present results within 7 business days after kickoff.
3) Schedule: Kickoff Tue 2026-07-06 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).

I'll circulate the calendar invite + Drive folder with the sweep tracker. If procurement needs an updated Dedicated quote we can provision a brief follow-up right after the sweep.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the kickoff.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
